response_kind: RFI response (capability statement, not a proposal)

card.situation:
DISA Sources Sought for Enterprise Messaging Modernization and Engineering Support — a 24/7/365 DevSecOps-driven effort to modernize DoD's enterprise messaging infrastructure across unclassified and classified environments, requiring WSDL-based services, publish/subscribe messaging, interoperability certifications, and a Secret Facility Clearance.
Reached the owner because Sooner Systems LLC matches the solicitation NAICS (541512), holds 22 Secret-cleared staff, and performs RMF/ATO and cybersecurity work — but the fit score of 0.39 and eight capability gaps flag this as a high-risk response candidate.
reasons_for: NAICS 541512 is an exact match and the firm qualifies as a small business well under the $34M size standard, making it eligible to respond to this unrestricted notice [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-fbc272fd].

RMF/ATO documentation, ACAS/Nessus vulnerability management, and CMMC Level 2 self-assessment directly address the RMF and cybersecurity compliance requirement, providing a credible partial narrative [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-2cf8c73d].

A 24x7 NOC and 22 Secret-cleared staff demonstrate continuous operational support capability and personnel readiness that partially align with the 24/7/365 support and clearance-level expectations [profile: 24x7 NOC; profile: 22 cleared staff (Secret)].
reasons_against: The firm has no Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) issued by the DCSA Facility Clearance Branch — individual staff clearances do not satisfy this threshold eligibility requirement [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-856025bd].

Eight of fourteen requirements are gaps, including the core technical disciplines — WSDL/SOA proficiency, publish/subscribe enterprise messaging, DevSecOps methodology, PDR/CDR engineering lifecycle, and classified DevSecOps environments — none of which appear anywhere in the firm's profile or past performance [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-199bb228; bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-c1f1cff7; bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-4e002a30; bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-fe67fa9b; bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-729531d2].

The firm holds no prime contract vehicles (ENCORE III, SETI, OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, etc.) and has no enterprise messaging or systems engineering past performance, leaving the capability statement unable to meet the two past-performance matches required by owner rule [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-5b1b2482; profile: owner rule ss-pp].

drafts.capability_statement:
To the Contracting Officer, Defense Information Systems Agency:

Sooner Systems LLC (SDVOSB, NAICS 541512) respectfully submits this capability statement in response to the Enterprise Messaging Modernization and Engineering Support Sources Sought notice (bb76a0d296574d508a645180aeaa8bc0).

Sooner Systems is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business registered under NAICS 541512, well within the $34M size standard. Our team of 22 Secret-cleared personnel supports continuous, mission-critical IT operations through a 24x7 Network Operations Center, directly aligned with DISA's requirement for 24/7/365 resilient infrastructure support.

Our cybersecurity and compliance capabilities include Risk Management Framework (RMF) and Authority to Operate (ATO) documentation, vulnerability management using ACAS and Nessus, Security+ certified staff, and CMMC Level 2 self-assessment — supporting the solicitation's RMF and cybersecurity compliance requirements. We have delivered network administration and cybersecurity support for federal customers including the FAA, encompassing RMF, ATO, ACAS, and STIG activities.

We also bring Microsoft 365 migration and systems administration experience, demonstrating familiarity with enterprise IT modernization efforts in federal environments.

Sooner Systems acknowledges capability gaps in WSDL-based service environments, publish/subscribe enterprise messaging platforms, DevSecOps toolchains, and classified development environments, and is actively evaluating teaming arrangements to address these areas for any subsequent solicitation.

We welcome the opportunity to discuss our capabilities further. Point of contact: [Owner to insert name, phone, and email before submission.]
questions_for_co: Facility Clearance [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-856025bd]: The notice states that contractors must have a final Secret Facility Clearance (FCL) from the DCSA Facility Clearance Branch at the time of proposal submission — will this FCL requirement apply equally at the Sources Sought / RFI response stage, or only at the time of a formal proposal submission under any subsequent solicitation?

WSDL and SOA Scope [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-199bb228]: Can DISA describe the extent to which WSDL-based service proficiency is required on day one of contract performance versus a capability that could be developed or transferred during a transition period, and whether teaming with a subcontractor holding this expertise would satisfy the requirement?

Publish/Subscribe Messaging Platforms [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-c1f1cff7]: Which enterprise messaging platforms or middleware (e.g., IBM MQ, Apache Kafka, XMPP, or a DISA-proprietary solution) currently underpin the EM capability, and will the contractor be expected to operate an existing platform, migrate to a new one, or both?

DevSecOps Environment Access [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-4e002a30; bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-729531d2]: Will DISA provide Government-furnished DevSecOps toolchains and classified environment infrastructure, or is the contractor expected to establish and accredit both unclassified and classified DevSecOps pipelines independently from contract award?

PDR/CDR Applicability [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-fe67fa9b]: Are Preliminary Design Reviews and Critical Design Reviews anticipated for the full modernization effort, for specific task orders, or only for discrete engineering change proposals — and does DISA anticipate issuing a Performance Work Statement or a Statement of Work/Objectives for the follow-on acquisition?

Contract Vehicle Requirement [bb76a0d2-896e1443-p1-5b1b2482]: Is possession of one of the listed prime contract vehicles (ENCORE III, SETI, OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, etc.) expected to be a mandatory eligibility requirement in the subsequent solicitation, or is the list provided solely for market research purposes to understand available ordering channels?

reader.scope_summary: DISA is seeking contractor support for the comprehensive lifecycle requirements of a modernized Enterprise Messaging (EM) capability that drives DoD information-sharing initiatives and Joint Information Environment goals. The effort requires continuous 24/7/365 support to ensure a resilient, scalable, and highly secure infrastructure, using a DevSecOps methodology across unclassified and classified environments. Contractors must support WSDL-based service environments, manage hierarchical messaging topics and channels, achieve interoperability certifications and information assurance accreditations, and comply with Risk Management Framework cybersecurity requirements.
quotes: DISA is seeking information, industry insights, and technical capability statements from potential, qualified vendors to support the comprehensive lifecycle requirements of a modernized EM capability.
Enterprise Messaging is a critical capability driving the Department of Defense (DoD) information-sharing initiatives and Joint Information Environment (JIE) goals.

the anticipated effort will require continuous 24/7/365 contractor support to ensure a resilient, scalable, and highly secure infrastructure aligned with DISA's operational standards and joint-warfighter requirements.

To be considered qualified and capable, Contractors must have a final Secret Facility Clearance from the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency Facility Clearance Branch at the time of proposal submission.

Interested parties must demonstrate proficiency in supporting environments where producers and consumers invoke services via a Web Services Description Language (WSDL) file, allowing clients and servers to communicate natively without forcing end-users to drastically modify their software base or convert to web-based languages.

The sustained solution must seamlessly support authorized publishers transmitting unaddressed messages—such as special reports, alerts, and briefs—while enabling authorized consumers to create synchronous or asynchronous subscriptions to these topics.
Additionally, the scope of this contract shall require the use of a DevSecOps methodology.
The respective unclassified and classified DevSecOps environments shall provide full end-to-end functionality.
The contractor shall achieve interoperability certifications and information assurance accreditations, while providing the support required to sustain the fielded solution.
Finally, all activities shall comply with Risk Management Framework (RMF), cybersecurity requirements and industry security best practices.
To make a determination for a small business set-aside, two or more qualified and capable small businesses must submit responses that demonstrate their qualifications.

SDVOSB set-aside eligibility (solicitation is currently unrestricted but status supports future set-aside response)
24x7 NOC demonstrates continuous operational support capability

ITIL 4 and Security+ certifications across the bench

No demonstrated proficiency in WSDL-based web services or service-oriented architecture
No experience with publish/subscribe enterprise messaging (unaddressed messages, synchronous/asynchronous subscriptions)

No interoperability certifications or IA accreditation experience beyond RMF/ATO documentation
No experience managing hierarchical messaging topics/channels or enterprise messaging platforms (e.g., MQ, Kafka, XMPP)
No classified DevSecOps environment experience mentioned
No prime contract vehicles listed (ENCORE III, SETI, NIH CIO-SP4, NASA SEWP V, GSA OASIS, ALLIANT II, VETS II, STARS III, MAS)
Owner rule [ss-pp] requires two past-performance matches — only marginal/partial matches exist; no true EM/messaging past performance
Scope is enterprise messaging modernization engineering — firm's profile is help desk and cybersecurity staffing, not software/systems engineering
